title: Signing Simon Edvinsson ‘remains a priority’ for Red Wings after Sweden return, Horcoff says
content:
Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said unsigned top-pair defenseman Simon Edvinsson “remains a priority” Friday, as the team’s negotiations with Edvinsson have dragged into the season and appear to be trending backward with the defenseman returning to Sweden earlier this week.

Edvinsson initially reported to the Red Wings training camp without a contract, as Detroit did not name a replacement for former general manager Steve Yzerman until September 15, when they elevated Horcoff to interim GM two days before the start of camp. But when Edvinsson and the team did not agree to a contract by the end of the preseason, Edvinsson was no longer practicing with the team on Monday, and on Wednesday Swedish journalist Andreas Johnsson posted video of him skating with Frölunda, the Gothenburg-based club from which he was drafted.

“He remains a priority,” Horcoff said Friday, shortly before the Red Wings season opener against the New York Rangers. “We’re doing everything (we) can, working closely with the agents. He’s a big part of our club and we’d like to get him signed. But the details of the negotiation, we’ll keep private between us, out of respect for Simon and his group, and we can comment on all of that when it’s all said and done.”

Asked if the Red Wings preferred a max-term or bridge deal, Horcoff reiterated, “We’re going to keep that until it’s all said and done.”

Horcoff did say that the team hadn’t expected Edvinsson to return to Sweden, saying, “We were excited when he came over (for camp), it was encouraging. … Of course it’s disappointing when he went back, but again, he’s a priority for us. We’re still working through this.”

Still, as for actual updates on the negotiations, the Red Wings’ interim general manager wasn’t interested in going into detail. It was similar on the subject of No. 1 center Dylan Larkin, whose trade request remains unresolved, with Horcoff saying “the focus with Dylan now is getting him healthy” from an upper-body injury.

“We want him to get healthy; he’s making great progress, skating with the team,” Horcoff said. “We think he’s close and once he is healthy, our priority is getting him back on the ice.”

Asked if teams were calling about Larkin and Edvinsson, Horcoff said: “They’re both elite players in the game, so I think any time there’s players like that that are talked about, it’s natural.”

Between Edvinsson, Larkin and leading scorer Alex DeBrincat entering the final year of his contract, Horcoff has a lot on his plate while carrying the interim tag — consequential decisions that will affect the Red Wings’ direction for years to come.

“This is a huge deal for me,” Horcoff said. “The Red Wings were my favorite team growing up; it was the first jersey that I ever owned. I went to Michigan State, my wife’s from Northville, this is home for us. To be in this position with the Red Wings really is a dream come true for me. I’m excited to put everything I have into this job. It’s a fantastic franchise, Original Six franchise, and this is just a massive honor for my family and I, and I’m excited for the challenge.”
